title: DevX Orbit: initiative timeline, risk matrix, and rollout playbook for SDK/docs/quickstarts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Create a single tracked initiative that coordinates SDK parity work, docs modernization, and quickstart templates so teams can measure activation lift and cycle-to-first-success. Scope covers iOS/Android/Node/Python SDKs, a new quickstarts repository (opinionated templates for common flows), and a docs hub rewrite focusing on 'first-success' journeys.

Success metrics (quarterly):
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS) reduced from 18m -> 6m for new signups (measured via funnel telemetry)
- SDK adoption: 30% increase in active SDK token usage from new signups within 14 days
- Quickstart conversion: 20% of users who complete a quickstart open an API key and call Redwood in 24 hours

Deliverables:
- SDK: two parity sprints (feature parity vs hosted API), single-source sample app for each stack (Node/Python/iOS/Android)
- Docs: task-driven hub, 6 canonical first-success paths, interactive code snippets with try-it-live sandbox
- Quickstarts: 4 opinionated templates (chat, embeddings search, reranker, summarize) with CI-driven sample tests

Why now / trade-offs:
- Prioritized because engineering usage telemetry shows onboarding friction is the dominant leak in conversion funnel. Trade-off: delaying minor runtime perf tickets to allocate eng effort to SDK parity.

Artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVX/DevX+Orbit+PRD, Prototype quickstarts repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devx-quickstarts, Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/devx-onboarding/first-success-funnel

Notes on tracking: We'll use a combined initiative board in Linear with weekly heatmap snapshots (traffic, TTFS, sample-run counts) and a monthly go/no-go checkpoint for canary rollouts of each quickstart template to the docs hub.
